stops.note: the general root for the desert-dwelling pack animal across Semitic languages
the Hebrew 'gamal' and Phoenician forms came to Greece through Levantine traders
Old English had borrowed 'camel' earlier from Latin, reinforced later by Norman French 'chamel'
settled as the English word, from Old English camel, reinforced by Old North French camel, both from Latin camelus
stops.meaning: a large desert-dwelling mammal with one or two humps

current_meaning: a large, humped mammal adapted for desert travel
